answer_1.quote: We present a simple yet novel testbed with: (i) an LLM personified as a lobbyist, proposing amendments in legislative bills ... The lobbyist's generation policy is parameterized through the memory encoding of the prompt augmented with a bill summary and business details of the target benefactor ...

answer_2.quote: We evaluate the two conflicting goals of the lobbyist as follows: (a) Identification Rate: ... (b) Benefit Capture Rate: The average of the lobbyist's evaluation score (S_eval) over all simulations, measuring the overall benefits captured in amendments.

answer_3.quote: Given only the amendments, the critic scores each candidate company ... we query the critic which of a pair (c1, c2) of companies benefit more ... convert to a spectral ranking using the Bradley‑Terry‑Luce model. The lobbyist uses this score to see if the amendment text t indeed gives the hidden benefit ... implemented by prompting the largest LLM with a yes/no choice.

answer_4.quote: We verify three important aspects for the quality of generations through human evaluations: 1. Benefit captured in the generated amendments ... 2. Verify the substantialness of the benefits planned by the lobbyist ... 3. Verify that the quality of re‑planning reasoning captures the intended benefits ... The evaluations were performed by 10 inhouse AI experts.
answer_4.guideline: Human raters assessed benefit capture, the substantialness of the benefits, and the quality of the re‑planning rationales.
